collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 12 District 4 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form (linked from portland.gov 2026 city candidates page); (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the two articles that profile every District 4 candidate: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 4 council race' (2026-10-07) and Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 4' (2026-09-11). Multi-winner race: OPB states three District 4 seats are on the ballot. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Ballot name 'Timothy (TJ) Anderson'; county guide file name uses 'Timothy (T.J.) Anderson'; OPB uses 'TJ Anderson'. Searches used 'Timothy Anderson'.
